key_insight: Introduce probabilistic feature imputation that produces uncertainty-aware representations for missing modalities, and use those uncertainty estimates to weight client contributions during federated aggregation, yielding more reliable multimodal models under modality heterogeneity.
problem_solved: Multimodal federated learning across healthcare sites where many clients lack one or more modalities; prior imputation methods give only point estimates and can make aggregation overconfident and unreliable.
method: Train a probabilistic feature imputer (outputs distributions / uncertainty for synthesized modality features) so missing modalities are represented as mean + uncertainty.
Propagate imputed-feature uncertainty through local models and communicate uncertainty-aware summaries (not just point features) to the server.
Perform uncertainty-aware federated aggregation that weights client contributions by imputation reliability, reducing influence of uncertain syntheses.
impact: Makes multimodal federated learning more robust and better-calibrated in realistic, heterogeneous clinical deployments—improving safety and trustworthiness when modalities are missing while preserving privacy.
visual_elements: System diagram: multiple clinics with partial modalities → probabilistic imputer at each client (shows mean + uncertainty) → server performing uncertainty-weighted aggregation to produce a global model.
Heatmap / mosaic showing modality availability across clients (high heterogeneity) to motivate the problem.
Line chart: downstream task performance vs. fraction of missing modalities comparing point-imputation vs. probabilistic imputation with uncertainty-aware aggregation.
Reliability diagram or bar chart showing calibration / reduction in overconfident errors when using uncertainty-aware aggregation.
paper_title: Probabilistic Feature Imputation and Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Federated Aggregation
paper_authors: Nafis Fuad Shahid, Maroof Ahmed, Md Akib Haider, Saidur Rahman Sagor, Aashnan Rahman
